AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER The closed session meeting was called to order by Mayor Lainez at 5:11pm

ROLL CALL City Clerk Sarmiento took roll call and noted that council member Rebollo was absent.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS No public comments were given for closed session agenda.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION Mayor Lainez recessed to closed session 5:15pm

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION Mayor Lainez reconvened the closed session meeting at 6:36 pm

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Noel Tapia provided his report from closed session. He stated that Council member Rebollo was not present from item one (1) of the closed session agenda. He also mentioned that item two (2) of the closed session was not discussed by city council. He continued with his report and stated that all five (5) city council members were present for the discussion of items three (3), four (4) and five (5). With regard to item three (3) staff provided a presentation, council gave direction and  there was no reportable action. With regard to item four (4) staff provided a presentation, council gave direction and there was no reportable action. With regard to item five (5) city council was given an update. That concluded the closed session report.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Lainez called the regular concurrent joint meetings of the City Council of the City of Commerce, Joint Powers Financing Authority and Governing Body to the Successor Agency to the Commerce Community Development Commission to order at 6:38 p.m.

ROLL CALL City Clerk Sarmiento took roll call and all members of the city council were present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Transportation Director Mc Ferguson led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION The invocation was offered by Mayor Pro Tem Mireya Garcia.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS Community Development Director Jessica Serrano provided a presentation regarding small business expo.

PUBLIC COMMENT The following people provided public comment.
Frank Martinez

CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Prior to city council taking action on the consent calendar City Attorney Tapia clarified that the agenda item on the consent calendar related to data centers is not about a data center project. The item on the agenda  is to provide a report on the uses and potential community impact related to data centers that is mandated by State law due to the councils adoption of an urgency ordinance enacting a 45 day moratorium on data centers. Council may also take action and extend the moratorium and additional ten (10) months and 15 days.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Yang provided a public safety report on behalf of the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department.

ORDINANCES

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Council Member Altamirano shared details of his attendance of the Commerce Scholarship event held at the Commerce Casino, and thanked those business and individuals who contributed to the scholarship funding. He also mention his attendance at the Teen Art Fest and thought it was remarkable and congratulated all the participants and proud parents in attendance.

Council Member Rebollo also shared details of her attendance at the Commerce Scholarship breakfast and mentioned how it is one of her favorite events because she gets an opportunity to see some of her previous scholars that she taught be recognized and receive funds to further their educations. She congratulated all the recipients and thanked all the local businesses for their generous and consistent annual contributions that keep the program going. She then mentioned the Back to School Bash and congratulated the Parks and Recreation department for putting on another successful event. She also mentioned her attendance at the Teen Art Fest and how impressed she was with the first annual event and how much she enjoyed seeing the amazing performances, artwork, and overall talent the Commerce community has to offer. She then mentioned her visit to Camp Commerce and see all the programming first hand and enjoyed the delicious food provided by the newly hired cook and encouraged residents to sign up. She congratulated camp staff for the great job they are doing and shared the positive response she received from residents who were a part of the trip. She closed by sharing a more somber report related to the passing of previous recreation lead Gabe Hannah and extended her and the city's condolences to his family. She also mentioned the passing of Santiago Medina was a well known and long time member of the senior clubs who recently passed away offered her condolences to his friends and family and requested the meeting be adjourned in both of their memories.

Council Member Argumedo also mentioned his attendance at the Back to School Bash event and congratulated staff for a successful event. He added how much the community enjoyed the festivities including the lucha libre matches. He then mentioned his attendance to the Local Cities Coalition and the I5 Cities Joint Power Authority meetings. He provided some details related to the meetings and stressed the importance of building a coalition that provides cities impacted by the freeway expansion more agency in how the project proceeds.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia mentioned her attendance at the Scholarship program and shared how nice of event it was. She thanked all the sponsors of program and shared her appreciation for their continued support and highlighted the great selection for made for the keynote speaker of the event that help to inspire our aspiring scholars. She also mentioned her attendance at the Teen Art Fest and shared how beautiful all of the art and performances were. She also mentioned receiving a yearbook style book from the dance team and thanked them for the kind gesture. She then mentioned her attendance at the Back to School Bash event and how much the community enjoyed the lucha libre matches. She then gave a shout out the senior center team and Margret in particular for taking care of our seniors and working through any and all situations. She closed by offering her deep condolences to the family of Gabe Hannah and Santiago Medina.

Mayor Lainez also mentioned his attendance at the Back to School Bash and how great of an event it was. He added how people really enjoyed the lucha libre matches the wrestlers ability to tell a story through physical performance. He also mentioned the musical performances by the day camp kids and thanked all the day campers and staff for the hard work they put in for the performances and the positive impact it has on the kids. He took time to acknowledge now former staff member of 27 years Gina Fierro who was an integral part of the day camp program and Parks and Recreation program. He wished Gina the best of luck and thanked her for her dedicated service to the Commerce community. He then mentioned the Scholarship breakfast event and concurred with his council colleague Rebollo that the event is one of the best of the year. He thanked library department and director Bautista and literacy services supervisor Evelyn Daiz for the great event. He added that 57 scholars received over $81,000 dollars in scholarships, and thanked the sponsors/donors and business community for their continued support and investment in the education of our youth. He singled out the Commerce Casino for their contribution of $50,000 dollars in scholarship funding. He then mentioned his attendance at the first annual Teen Art Fest and said the event was a success. He gave kudos to the teen center staff lead by Amber Torres for the well organized event that showcased the amazing performances, artwork and talent of Commerce youth. He also mentioned his attendance at the LAFC game organized by the department of Parks and Recreation and thanked staff for organizing the event. He then provided information on the Small Business Expo set for September 2, 2026 from 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m and thanked the city council for moving forward on the Commerce Advantage program which will help to continue encouraging small business growth in Commerce. Mayor Lainez closed his report by sharing his condolences to the families of Gabe Hannah and Santiago Media.

ADJOURNMENT Mayor Lainez adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Gabe Hannah and Santiago Media at 8:16 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

WASHINGTON BOULEVARD.  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Community Development Director Jessica Serrano introduced the public hearing item and provided a presentation.

Mayor Lainez opened the public hearing at 7:50 p.m.

Public comment was provided by Frank Martinez related to the item.

Mayor Lainez closed the public hearing at 7:52 p.m.

Prior to the City Council taking action on the item, city attorney Tapia read aloud the recommended additional conditions of approval requirements for the record. Those requirements are:

1. The applicant shall be required to prevent the consumption of alcohol on the premises.

2. The applicant shall cause anyone consuming alcohol to leave the premises and will call law enforcement for assistance.
